Unofficial integration: it prices your electricity in Gladys with the **grid
tariff of your Norwegian grid company** (nettleie), the public charges and,
if you want, the spot price with the **strømstøtte** or **Norgespris**. It is
not affiliated with any grid company, with NVE, with Hva koster strømmen.no
or with the fri-nettleie project.

> This integration has never been tested with a real Gladys contract and a
> real meter in Norway: the prices are checked against the published tariffs
> by its tests, not against a real bill. Tell us what you see.

## What it does

- A contract template **"Nettleie (Norway)"** (delegated pricing, Gladys 5.3
  or later): Gladys sends the consumption of each half hour, the integration
  answers its cost in NOK, VAT included:
  - the **energy part** (energiledd) of your company's tariff for that local
    hour, day type (working day, weekend, public holiday) and month;
  - the **consumption tax** (forbruksavgift) and the **Enova levy**
    (1 øre/kWh), and **25 % VAT** in the south zone;
  - with the **spot** supply: the hourly day-ahead price of your area plus your
    supplier's markup, minus the **strømstøtte** (90 % of the hourly spot
    price above 77 øre/kWh without VAT in 2026, 75 øre in 2025, at most
    5,000 kWh a month, households only);
  - with the **Norgespris** supply: 40 øre/kWh without VAT plus your markup,
    within 5,000 kWh a month (1,000 for a holiday home), the spot price
    beyond. The scheme runs from 1 October 2025 to 31 December 2029, but its
    price is only set for 2025 and 2026 (40 øre): from 1 January 2027 the half
    hours get no cost until an update of the integration carries the new
    price.
- One device per contract (in **Discovery** once the contract exists): the
  **price now** (NOK/kWh), the **capacity peak of the month** (kW), the
  **capacity step** reached (NOK/month, VAT included) and the threshold of
  the **next step** (kW): enough for a scene that warns before a new step.
- A **Test** button: the company found, the date of its data, the price now,
  the capacity of the month, and a comparison of today's tariff with what
  NVE holds.

## The capacity step (kapasitetsledd)

Every Norwegian grid company bills a monthly fixed part by **steps of
power**, most of them from the mean of the three highest hours of the month,
on three different days. The Gladys pricing engine **cannot bill a step**:
its "demand" component is a price per kW (a straight line, not steps), and a
delegated cost is the energy only. So the integration does not hide it in the
kWh price; instead:

- the contract device **shows** the peak of the month (computed from the
  half-hour consumption Gladys sends for pricing: kWh of each clock hour, mean
  of the three highest days) and the step it reaches;
- the template has an optional **"Capacity step per month"** input, counted by
  Gladys as a fixed monthly amount: enter the step you expect if you want it
  in the totals.

Steps computed: the common rule (TRE_DØGNMAX_MND) and the highest hour of the
month (MND_MAX). Companies billing on the five highest weeks of the year or
on the fuse size (FEM_VEKTET_ÅR, OV_TREFASE) have no computed step: the Test
button says so. The peak only counts the half hours Gladys has priced: a gap
in the meter data lowers it.

## Set up

1. Install the integration. Nothing to fill in its configuration.
2. In **Energy > Contracts**, create a contract on your main meter with the
   **"Nettleie (Norway)"** template and fill its inputs:
   - **Grid company**: its name ("Elvia"), its fri-nettleie file name (the
     list below), its GLN or its organisation number;
   - **Customer group**: household, or holiday_home (fritidsbolig);
   - **Tax zone**: south, north (Nordland, Troms: no VAT) or tiltakssone
     (Finnmark and the Nord-Troms municipalities: no VAT, no consumption
     tax);
   - **Electricity supply**: grid_only, spot or norgespris, and the **price
     area** (NO1 to NO5) for the last two (required: no default);
   - **Supplier markup** (påslag, NOK/kWh without VAT), **capacity step** and
     **other monthly fees** (NOK/month with VAT), all optional.
3. In **Discovery**, add the contract device if you want its sensors.
4. Press **Test** in the configuration screen.

A wrong input never becomes a default: the half hours get no cost, the
status names the input, and Gladys asks again at its next run once it is
fixed. The status also warns when the tax zone does not match the county of
the company, and when the tariff in force dates from an earlier year and the
company's file was not checked this year (its prices are still used, not
verified this year). The monthly caps of the
strømstøtte and Norgespris count the kWh Gladys sends since the start of
the month, or since the contract start when later: start the contract on
the 1st of a month. A company with several tariffs at once (one file has them in its
history) asks for the **Tariff name**: the status lists the choices.

## Where the data comes from, and how fresh it is

- **Grid tariffs and tax rates: fri-nettleie**
  ([https://github.com/kraftsystemet/fri-nettleie](https://github.com/kraftsystemet/fri-nettleie)), a community collection
  of the tariffs of every Norwegian grid company, by **Fri nettleie /
  kraftsystemet**, data under **CC BY 4.0**
  ([https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)). The integration ships a
  copy (commit 58a0d20, 10 November 2026) and, once a day, reads again the
  files of the companies your contracts use (conditional request, nothing
  sent but the file name; switch off in the configuration). The status and
  the Test button show the **date of the data** (the "sist_oppdatert" of the
  company's file). Changes made: the tariffs are checked field by field, the
  yearly capacity prices are shown per month, taxes and VAT are added.
- **Comparison: NVE**, the tariffs the companies report to the regulator
  ([https://nettleietariffer.dataplattform.nve.no](https://nettleietariffer.dataplattform.nve.no)), only by the Test button,
  at most once per company and hour. Contains data under the Norwegian
  Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) made available by NVE
  ([https://data.norge.no/nlod/](https://data.norge.no/nlod/)). NVE is sometimes months behind: the prices
  always follow fri-nettleie.
- **Spot prices: Strømpriser levert av Hva koster strømmen.no**
  ([https://www.hvakosterstrommen.no](https://www.hvakosterstrommen.no), open API, free for any use; only for
  the spot and Norgespris supplies). Hourly ENTSO-E day-ahead prices
  converted to NOK by the site with the Norges Bank rate of the day: they can
  differ slightly from the NOK prices of Nord Pool and of your bill. History
  from 1 December 2021; a day is kept only whole (23, 24 or 25 hours), for
  62 days. The pricing never waits for them: a half hour whose spot price is
  not held yet gets no cost at once, the day is read in the background and
  Gladys prices it at its next run. Gladys needs a cost for every half hour
  of a request: a day the source does not have leaves the half hours not yet
  priced of the same billing period without cost (Gladys catches up 31 days at
  most), and the status names the day. Such a day is asked again every 6
  hours.
- **Strømstøtte and Norgespris rules**: from the regulation (FOR-2025-09-08-1791)
  and the government pages, checked against the Strømkalkulator project
  (MIT). They are written in the integration with their dates: after 2026,
  or for a year whose tax rates fri-nettleie has not published yet, the half
  hours get **no cost** (never a guessed one) until the data is there. The
  tax rates come from a file of fri-nettleie's collection guide
  (`satser.yml`): if the project moves it, the shipped rates stay and the
  following year has no cost until an update.

## Good to know

- All times are Norway's local time (Europe/Oslo). On the night the clocks go
  back, both 02:00 hours are "hour 2", as the companies count.
- The strømstøtte is computed hour by hour on the hourly spot price; a half
  hour takes the price of its hour (Gladys sends half hours).
- A total below zero (negative spot price) counts as zero: Gladys does not
  take a credit.
- The integration sends nothing about you anywhere: it reads public files.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Nettleie (Norway) te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Norwegian grid tariffs | `section` | No | This integration prices your electricity with the grid tariff of your company: create a contract with the "Nettleie (Norway)" template in Energy > Contracts and enter your grid company there. Tariffs: fri-nettleie (kraftsystemet, CC BY 4.0), shipped with the integration and read again once a day from GitHub. Spot prices (only for the "spot" and "Norgespris" supplies): Strømpriser levert av Hva koster strømmen.no (ENTSO-E day-ahead, in NOK). The capacity step (kapasitetsledd) is shown by the contract device, not added to the costs: see the documentation. |
| Read the tariffs again every day | `boolean` | No | Once a day, the files of the grid companies your contracts use (and the tax rates) are read again from the fri-nettleie repository on GitHub. Off: only the data shipped with this version. |

## Cómo instalar Nettleie (Norway) en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Nettleie (Norway) aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-nettleie:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-nettleie](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-nettleie).

Nettleie (Norway) requiere Gladys `>=5.3.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Nettleie (Norway) es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
